lexemes.note: The present-tense negation of existence and possession (the opposite of יֵשׁ). Formal Hebrew also inflects it as a negative copula: אֵינֶנִּי / אֵינִי, אֵינְךָ, אֵינוֹ, אֵינָהּ …

profile.feeling: Absence: no milk, no time, no problem.

senses.def: there is not, there are no; with לְ: not to have — the negation of יֵשׁ
is not (formal negative copula, often with a suffix: אֵינוֹ, אֵינָהּ)

examples.tr: There is no milk in the fridge.

phrases.tr: there is nothing new under the sun

phrases.meaning: never mind; it’s nothing (a reply to thanks or an apology)

synonyms.nuance: the general “not” for verbs, adjectives and the past/future; אֵין is only for “there isn’t / don’t have” in the present (and formal negative copula)

etymology.text: Compare Ugaritic 𐎛𐎐 (ỉn) and Arabic إِنْ (ʔin).

funFacts: The mystical name אֵין סוֹף (Ein Sof, “the Infinite”) is literally “there is no end”.
Same letters, a different word: אַיִן “nothing, nothingness” (as in יֵשׁ מֵאַיִן).
pitfalls: Never *לֹא יֵשׁ — say אֵין: אֵין לִי גֶּזֶר.
Present only: “there wasn’t” = לֹא הָיָה, “there won’t be” = לֹא יִהְיֶה.
subtleties: Formal style negates a present verb with אֵין + suffix: אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ “I do not know”; everyday speech says אֲנִי לֹא יוֹדֵעַ.

senses.def: not (negates verbs, adjectives, adverbs and whole predicates)

synonyms.nuance: the “not” of prohibitions, with the future: אַל תִּקְנֶה! “don’t buy!”

etymology.text: From Proto-Semitic *lā. Cognate with Arabic لا.

funFacts: Arabic لا (lā) is the same word: both “not” and “no”.
pitfalls: לֹא stands right before what it negates: הוּא לֹא אוֹכֵל (not after the verb).
For “there isn’t / I don’t have” use אֵין, not לֹא: אֵין לִי זְמַן.
subtleties: Negative words still need לֹא: אֲנִי לֹא רוֹצֶה כְּלוּם “I want nothing” (literally “I don’t want nothing”).
לֹא + future is an absolute prohibition, as in the Ten Commandments: לֹא תִּרְצָח.
